method: Automated inventory read every source, evidence, pathway, profile and review record in the exact manifest candidate for this ISO.

Automated screening compared source references, locators, geography fields, evidence class, direction, status, horizon and scenario; it checked pathway support IDs, link-evidence sets, geography fields, alternatives and uncertainty for follow-up.

Raw extraction access rows are recorded only as inherited access observations. This generated screen does not treat snippets, HTTP success, prior access, or metadata as claim verification and does not replace semantic source review.

evidence.compact_statement: Source dated 2025-11 reports: The CCDR records over 152 deaths and US$1.2 billion in losses from hazards over decades; landslides led to dozens of villages abandoned or displaced in 40 years. Shovi’s 2023 debris flow in Racha killed at least 32 and affected over 200.
recommendations: No wording change is indicated by the record-only check; keep the claim provisional until its cited passage is independently reopened.

evidence.compact_statement: Source dated 2025-11 reports: Among 100-year-flood-exposed people, 12% are poor and 77% have multiple vulnerabilities; among drought-exposed people, 12.1% are poor and 80% have multiple vulnerabilities. Kakheti is most drought-exposed; 91% there face other vulnerabilities.
recommendations: No wording change is indicated by the record-only check; keep the claim provisional until its cited passage is independently reopened.

evidence.compact_statement: The 2025 CCDR models higher food-price-related poverty under a dry/hot scenario than under stated policies, with particularly adverse consumption effects in Imereti, Mtskheta-Mtianeti, Samegrelo-Zemo Svaneti and Kakheti. These are scenario results, not observed poverty changes.
recommendations: No wording change is indicated by the record-only check; keep the claim provisional until its cited passage is independently reopened.

evidence.compact_statement: Source dated 2025 reports: The UN analysis places spatial, social, political (including unresolved conflict) and environmental (including climate) factors among intersecting sources of vulnerability. Conflict disproportionately affects forcibly displaced people, residents outside government control and communities near Abkhazia/South Ossetia ABLs.
recommendations: No wording change is indicated by the record-only check; keep the claim provisional until its cited passage is independently reopened.

evidence.compact_statement: Source dated 2025 reports: Isolated mountain communities have limited development and inadequate infrastructure; older women in small-scale agriculture are particularly climate-vulnerable.
recommendations: No wording change is indicated by the record-only check; keep the claim provisional until its cited passage is independently reopened.

evidence.compact_statement: Source dated 2025 reports: Monitoring, mapping, climate forecasting and early warnings have improved, but agricultural warnings and insurance remain weak; emergency social protection roles are unclear, with limited capacity to add beneficiaries or use municipalities as first responders.
recommendations: No wording change is indicated by the record-only check; keep the claim provisional until its cited passage is independently reopened.

evidence.compact_statement: Source dated 2025-12 reports: By mid-century, heat risk covers Kvemo Kartli, Kakheti and the coast under SSP1-2.6, expanding across Kolkheti Plain under SSP3-7.0; mountainous areas face more days above 25°C under SSP3-7.0.
recommendations: No wording change is indicated by the record-only check; keep the claim provisional until its cited passage is independently reopened.

affected_groups: communities and water users in the Kura-Aras Basin
evidence.compact_statement: Source dated 2025-12 reports: SSP3-7.0 projects less summer rain in the Kura-Aras Basin by mid-century, raising water-shortage and hydrological-drought risks that could prompt water-use conflict.
recommendations: No wording change is indicated by the record-only check; keep the claim provisional until its cited passage is independently reopened.

evidence.compact_statement: Source dated 2025-12 reports: Climate impacts compound displacement linked to episodic conflict and violence. IDPs face inadequate housing, limited services and livelihoods, plus heightened flood, drought and resource risks; much of Georgia is listed among areas with many IDPs.
recommendations: Retain explicitly as a regional South Caucasus profile; do not imply the general climate-risk passage is mapped specifically within Georgia.

evidence.compact_statement: Source dated 2020-11 reports: The 2020 assessment says historic wetland drainage worsens lowland flood risk and is linked to coastal erosion, particularly around Poti; dams and port works also disrupt sediment delivery, including from Khobistskali, contributing to erosion and sediment accumulation at Poti port.
recommendations: No wording change is indicated by the record-only check; keep the claim provisional until its cited passage is independently reopened.

pathways.compact_statement: Conflict-related displacement and inadequate housing/services can magnify climate-hazard vulnerability in Georgia; no climate-caused conflict claim.
alternative_explanations: Poverty, building quality and hazard exposure also shape losses independently of displacement.
Regional synthesis is not a matched local comparison.
pathways.uncertainty: Source-stated vulnerability mechanism, not causal identification; do not assign uniform exposure to all IDPs or named conflict territories.
recommendations: Keep the reverse mechanism bounded to the named institution, population and place supported by its cited evidence; do not infer violence from climate vulnerability.
